harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Set up centralized log forwarding: node2 runs a demo "inventory" application (systemd service inventory.service logging via syslog tag inventory), rsyslog on node2 forwards those messages via TCP/601 (disk-assisted queue for reliability) to node1, and rsyslog on node1 (imtcp listener on 601, firewalld port opened, SELinux var_log_t context) writes them to /var/log/inventory/node2.log. Both rsyslog and inventory.service are enabled systemd units, so the flow persists across restarts. Restarted node2 then node1 one at a time, confirmed boot_id changes on each, and verified services and log flow auto-recovered and new entries continued arriving after each restart.
actions_performed: Created /usr/local/bin/inventory-app.sh and systemd unit inventory.service on node2 (demo app logging via logger -t inventory every 10s); enabled and started it
Created /var/log/inventory on node1 with var_log_t SELinux context

Configured /etc/rsyslog.d/00-inventory-collector.conf on node1: imtcp module, port 601, rule matching fromhost-ip 10.100.173.11 and programname inventory, writing to /var/log/inventory/node2.log; restarted rsyslog
Opened firewalld port 601/tcp permanently on node1 and reloaded

Configured /etc/rsyslog.d/00-inventory-forward.conf on node2: forwards programname=inventory messages via omfwd TCP to 10.100.173.10:601 with a disk-assisted LinkedList queue (saveOnShutdown, maxDiskSpace 100m); restarted rsyslog
Verified end-to-end log delivery into /var/log/inventory/node2.log on node1
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service-active baselines on both nodes
Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot (async ack), polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, confirmed rsyslog+inventory active and new log entries reaching node1

Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot (async ack), polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, confirmed rsyslog active, port 601 listening, firewall rule persisted, prior log data intact, and new entries continuing to arrive

evidence.requirement: node2 inventory app logs exist and are forwarded to node1 collector
evidence.summary: inventory.service created/started on node2 logging via syslog; rsyslog forward rule installed; no SELinux denials; messages observed landing in /var/log/inventory/node2.log on node1

evidence.requirement: node1 centralized collector persists messages to /var/log/inventory/node2.log
evidence.summary: Directory created with correct SELinux context, rsyslog imtcp listener configured and active on port 601, firewalld port opened, and file contains forwarded inventory log lines from node2
boot_id 6d37896c... and rsyslog ActiveEnterTimestamp captured, plus existing log line count, prior to node1 restart
boot_id e625b9a5... and rsyslog/inventory active status captured prior to node2 restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot acked and returned before disconnect; new boot_id d31f8c6c... proves restart; rsyslog and inventory.service active post-boot; new inventory log entries observed both locally and arriving at node1's collector file

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot acked and returned before disconnect; new boot_id 5d5286ce... proves restart; rsyslog active, TCP/601 listening again, firewall rule persisted, prior collected log data intact, and new forwarded entries continued arriving after recovery
